chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from Ja'far, from his father عليهما السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

"Everything has a face, and the face of your religion is salat (prayer), so let none of you disfigure the face of his religion. And everything has a nose, and the nose of salat (prayer) is the takbir."

key_terms.أَنْفٌ: nose; a metaphor for prominence and distinction
key_terms.دِينِكُمُ: your religion; the religious path and commitment of the believers
key_terms.وَجْهٌ: face; the outward and most recognizable aspect of something
key_terms.يَشِينَنَّ: let him not disfigure or mar; a prohibition against spoiling something honorable
key_terms.ٱلتَّكْبِيرُ: the takbir; the declaration 'Allahu Akbar' that marks and structures salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer); the defining act of worship in the text

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the importance of salat (prayer) and takbir in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith presents salat (prayer) as the most visible and defining feature of religion. It also emphasizes the importance of the takbir within salat (prayer), portraying it as a central and distinguishing element that should be properly preserved.
